short: A piece that cannot move without exposing something more valuable behind it.
body: An absolute pin is against the king: the pinned piece legally cannot move. A relative pin is against anything else — usually the queen — and the pinned piece absolutely can move, if moving it creates a bigger threat than the thing behind it is worth.
That distinction decides games. Legal's Mate works precisely because a knight 'pinned' to the queen moves anyway and delivers mate with three minor pieces while the queen sits untouched.
So whenever you rely on a pin, check which kind it is. If it is relative, ask what your opponent gets by ignoring it.

diagram.caption: The bishop on g4 pins the knight to the queen. That pin is relative, not absolute.
